recipes.name: Pork Chops Italiano
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced Italian tomatoes, undrained

steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in mushrooms; cook and stir until tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and set aside until needed.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add pork chops and cook until browned, 3 ½ to 5 minutes per side; transfer to a plate. Drain all but 1 tablespoon drippings from the skillet.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet; cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper.

Add pork chops and simmer until tender and no longer pink in the center, about 45 minutes, adding water if mixture becomes too dry. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of each pork chop should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
Place a bell pepper slice on top of each pork chop. Add reserved mushrooms and continue to simmer until peppers are tender, 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Chops Italiano
raw_recipe.description: Pork chops, peppers, mushrooms, and tomatoes are simmered in a savory sauce in this easy recipe that brings tons of Italian flavor to the table.

video.description: Charge up the flavor on your favorite pork chops with simmered onions, garlic and tomatoes along with some basil, oregano and a topping of mushrooms and bell pepper. After you cook your mushrooms and brown your pork chops, the rest of the ingredients join up and simmer, for a delicious entrée in about an hour. Serve with a side of noodles or polenta, and a side salad, and dinner’s done!

review.reviewBody: The secret to moist pork chops is to use bone in chops. The boneless chops dry out during the simmering process.

Supper slow and low… I just made it… doubled all the seasoning… going to try triple next time… flavors were still pretty low. I used really thick chops… sear, sear… then to better control my low temp and give more flavor/cook time… I used a crock pot. I got what I was looking for… super tender fall off the bone chops that were full of juices and flavoring from the Diced tomatoes, a can of rotell, with a can of tomato paste or 2. So more spices next time… but still awfully good now that I figured out how to get the juices to the middle of the meat. THICK CHOPS! 6hrs slow and low. Also tried on a bed of rice and a bed of noodles. Both work well. This summer, started the chops in a giant iron skillet on the stove top. Then moved over to the grill, slow and low. Not over direct heat. Finished them off by smoking them for a bit…. Must try with a little smoke.

I've been making this for a couple years now. I always do something different. Tonight I'm using bone-in, skinless thighs; seasoned w/ garlic salt, lemon pepper, & italian seasoning prior to searing; added better than bouillon italian herb base; instead of water, used red wine to increase the liquid. Orzo on the side. Always a hit w/ the family.

Really enjoyed the flavor. We had it over jasmine rice. Only change was browned 5 pork loin chops in a cast iron pan and cubed them. Also added a can of Rotel. I let it simmer for about 10 minutes then pressure cooked it on high in the instant pot 15 minutes. The pork was tender and juicy. Will make again.

I made these in my instant pot - I rubbed the oregano, basil, salt, and pepper on my pork chops, sautéed in oil for about 3 minutes. Added the onion, garlic and tomatoes sautéed another minute. Cooked on high pressure for 30 minutes (thick pork chops). Quick release on the pressure and added the bell peppers and mushrooms for 2 minutes on high. One word...Amazing!

I liked this! I did some extra stuff though… I brined my pork for 3 hours in garlic, fresh rosemary, fresh thyme, salt and sugar. I seasoned the mushrooms and onions as I went. Be careful not to add too much salt if you season each ingredient. It’ll turn out too salty. I also used fire roasted garlic diced tomatoes. I made this is my cast iron Dutch oven so it didn’t take the full 45 mins. Keep temping your pork as you go so as not to overcook it. Pork dries out easily, even when brined. Overall, would make again. I also only used 2 chops and the amount of sauce wasn’t insane. 4 stars because I did some tweaks but overall a good recipe!

I had boneless porkchops, so I did not simmer 45min. 15 minutes did the trick. I also seasoned the chops before cooking them, after reading some of the reviews. I served this with mashed potatoes, but I think it is very versatile and quinoa, egg noodles, or rice would be good too. I will definitely be cooking this again!

Turned out great! Pork was a bone in so it stayed moist! Flavors were great but I added salt, pepper and onion powder to the raw chops before searing! I put it with a garlic quinoa and green salad! Awesome meal!

This recipe was very, very good. Made it as is just changed the order of the cooking: braised the pork first then the mushrooms, and last the onions and garlic. I also deglazed the pan with a splash of white wine. I served it with Parmesan Garlic Orzo from this site and honestly, it was fantastic! Will make it again. You can opt for just serving it over cooked orzo. The recipe leaves enough sauce to mix with the orzo or any other shaped pasta of your choosing.

I jus made this recipe tonight for my family and it was a big hit.. I followed the directions all except the simmering time.. instead of 45 I did 25.. n then added the peppers and mushrooms for 10 extra minutes.. so all together i let the chops simmer for 35 minutes.. I also used the bone-in chops because after reading the reviews it seemed to be the better choice.. plus it was already n my freezer.. lol.. oh and I used some red wine to make sure nothing dried out..I finished it off with some basil pesto pasta, green beans yellow beans and carrots... the meat was so tender and juicy.. n the pasta tasted even better once it was glazed over with the sauce.. definitely looking forward to making this again..

I made this recipe because I saw it featured in the Allrecipes Greatest Hits. I am always looking for grain-free recipes without sugar, and this recipe filled the bill! It was delicious with red bell pepper, but multi-colored would probably be a good idea, too. The chops were tender and juicy, and the Italian-inspired sauce was a nice change for a weeknight pork chop. Besides the red pepper instead of green, I kept the skillet uncovered after adding the mushrooms, to reduce the sauce a bit. I will definitely make again. Thanks, lutzflcat!
It was delicious. I will make it again.

Very good. Left out the mushrooms as I don’t like them. Only made 2 bone in large center cut pork chops and it was just enough sauce for two. I used better than bouillon chicken for the 1/2 cup water. Will definitely make these again as it is a very easy recipe.
My husband didn't like it.
Next time, no pepper on pork chops, no more than 8 pork cops so as not to crowd the pan. 20 ozs of diced, seasoned tomatoes. Try for slightly thicker chops.
Great, easy recipe. Bone-in chops will probably taste great, but i prefer boneless pork loin for a lower fat option. Finished dish is great served over a bed of rice, & the sauce makes a great gravy!
Just wonderfully flavored together with my homemade mashed potatoes 🥴
Tried something new for speghetti night, left out the peppers and it was delicious. Will be making this again.
I think the only change I'd make is sauté the peppers. However, this is very good and tastes better the next day!
Looks very tasty and great
